sources.cite: AWS. SageMaker AI Developer Guide: Auto scaling policy overview
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: target tracking 'adds and removes the number of instances as required to keep the metric at, or close to, the specified target value'; default scale-in and scale-out cooldown 300 seconds each; 'You can manually scale out by increasing the minimum value'; 'SageMaker AI auto scaling does not enforce a limit' for the maximum.

sources.cite: AWS. SageMaker AI Developer Guide: Define a scaling policy
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: predefined metric types SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance and SageMakerVariantConcurrentRequestsPerModelHighResolution; the high-resolution metrics 'emit data every 10 seconds' so the policy scales out 'much more quickly' while it scales in 'at the same speed' as standard metrics, which emit once a minute.

sources.cite: AWS. SageMaker AI Developer Guide: Load testing your auto scaling configuration
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance = (MAX_RPS * SAFETY_FACTOR) * 60; 'SageMaker AI recommends that you start testing with a SAFETY_FACTOR of 0.5'; multiply by 60 for the per-minute metric.

sources.cite: AWS. SageMaker AI Developer Guide: Amazon SageMaker AI metrics in CloudWatch
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: ModelLatency in microseconds; InvocationsPerInstance normalized by instance count; Invocation5XXErrors; ConcurrentRequestsPerModel 'The number of concurrent requests being received by the model'; CPUUtilization is the sum over cores, 0-400% on four vCPUs.

sources.cite: AWS. Application Auto Scaling User Guide: Scheduled scaling
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: scheduled actions 'increase or decrease capacity at specific times' by changing minimum and maximum capacity; used with scaling policies, 'the scaling policy can continue to make decisions'. The page does not name SageMaker; endpoint variants are Application Auto Scaling scalable targets (SageMaker auto scaling prerequisites page, read the same day).
